<|start|>user<|message|>An airport baggage router moves suitcases between three sorting stations arranged in a ring. A single control token circulates around the ring, and only the station currently holding the token may append a scan event to the shared manifest record. When a station holds the token it records exactly one scan by incrementing both its own local tally and the shared manifest counter, then it may later pass the token to its ring successor. Because the conveyor network can reorder low-level messages, the token may sit at a station for several steps before moving on. The design must guarantee that the shared manifest never loses or duplicates a scan: the manifest counter always equals the sum of every station's local tally. Scanning stops once the daily cap of events is reached.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared manifest counter always equals the sum of all stations' individual scan tallies, so no update is ever lost.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m1p1t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS N, Cap
VARIABLES token, manifest, tally
vars == <<token, manifest, tally>>
Stations == 0 .. (N - 1)
RECURSIVE SumOver(_)
SumOver(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
              ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN tally[x] + SumOver(S \ {x})
Init == token = 0 /\ manifest = 0 /\ tally = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
Scan == manifest < Cap
        /\ manifest' = manifest + 1
        /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![token] = @ + 1]
        /\ token' = token
Pass == token' = (token + 1) % N /\ manifest' = manifest /\ tally' = tally
Next == Scan \/ Pass
NoLostUpdate == manifest = SumOver(Stations)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
```
```cfg
CONSTANTS N = 3  Cap = 4
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A hospital operating-room scheduler keeps a bounded queue of pending surgeries and dispatches them to a single on-call anesthesiologist. Cases are admitted to the queue only while it is below its capacity, which provides backpressure to the intake desk. The currently authorized anesthesiologist carries a shift token equal to the scheduler's shift counter; at a handover the counter advances and the incoming clinician's token is refreshed. A clinician may pull and start the next case only when their carried token still matches the live shift counter, so a slow but not failed clinician whose shift already rotated cannot start a case. The scheduler records which shift token last started a case. The safety requirement is that any started case was started under the current shift authorization, never by a stale participant.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shift token that last started a case is always equal to the scheduler's current shift counter, so no stale clinician ever starts a case.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m4p6t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Cap, MaxShift
VARIABLES queue, shift, clinicianTok, lastStartTok
vars == <<queue, shift, clinicianTok, lastStartTok>>
Init == queue = 0 /\ shift = 0 /\ clinicianTok = 0 /\ lastStartTok = 0
Admit == queue < Cap /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<shift, clinicianTok, lastStartTok>>
Start == queue > 0 /\ clinicianTok = shift
         /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ lastStartTok' = clinicianTok
         /\ UNCHANGED <<shift, clinicianTok>>
Handover == shift < MaxShift /\ shift' = shift + 1 /\ clinicianTok' = shift + 1
            /\ lastStartTok' = shift + 1 /\ UNCHANGED queue
Next == Admit \/ Start \/ Handover
OnlyAuthorizedServes == lastStartTok = shift
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
```
```cfg
CONSTANTS Cap = 3  MaxShift = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyAuthorizedServes
```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A warehouse robot fleet coordinates access to a shared charging bay using leases. At most one robot holds the bay at a time, and it holds a lease with a remaining time-to-live. On each tick the lease's time-to-live decreases, and when it reaches zero the lease expires and the bay becomes free. Because control messages can be reordered, a robot must never perform bay work under an expired lease. A free bay can be granted to any waiting robot with a fresh time-to-live. The safety requirement is that whenever the bay is held, its lease still has strictly positive time-to-live, so no robot ever acts on a stale, expired lease.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the charging bay has an owner, its lease time-to-live is strictly positive, so no robot ever holds the bay under an expired lease.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m6p6t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Robots, MaxTTL
VARIABLES owner, ttl
vars == <<owner, ttl>>
NONE == "none"
Init == owner = NONE /\ ttl = 0
Grant == owner = NONE /\ \E r \in Robots : owner' = r /\ ttl' = MaxTTL
Tick == owner # NONE /\ ttl > 1 /\ ttl' = ttl - 1 /\ owner' = owner
Expire == owner # NONE /\ ttl = 1 /\ owner' = NONE /\ ttl' = 0
Next == Grant \/ Tick \/ Expire
HolderLeaseValid == (owner # NONE) => (ttl > 0)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
```
```cfg
CONSTANTS Robots = {r1, r2}  MaxTTL = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT HolderLeaseValid
```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A bank's interbank settlement service runs batches using two-phase commit across a set of participants. A coordinator opens a round, collects votes, and only commits when every participant in the round has voted yes. Each committed batch is stamped with the round number under which it was decided. Two independent settlement instances draw from one shared round pool, so a stale coordinator from an earlier round must never stamp a commit. When a new round opens the round number advances and any partial voting resets. The safety requirement is that the round stamp on the most recent committed batch always equals the currently open round, so no stale coordinator commits.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The round number stamped on the last committed batch always equals the currently open round number, so no stale coordinator ever commits a batch.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m2p6t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Participants, MaxRound
VARIABLES round, yes, committedRound
vars == <<round, yes, committedRound>>
Init == round = 0 /\ yes = {} /\ committedRound = 0
Vote == \E p \in Participants : p \notin yes /\ yes' = yes \cup {p}
        /\ UNCHANGED <<round, committedRound>>
Commit == yes = Participants /\ committedRound' = round /\ yes' = {}
          /\ UNCHANGED round
OpenRound == round < MaxRound /\ round' = round + 1 /\ yes' = {}
             /\ committedRound' = round + 1
Next == Vote \/ Commit \/ OpenRound
CommitMatchesRound == committedRound = round
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
```

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CommitMatchesRound
```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A university course-registration system tracks the seats of one popular course using a compare-and-swap register. The course has a total seat pool that is split between seats still free and seats already taken. A student enrolls by a compare-and-swap that moves one seat from free to taken; a student who drops moves one seat back. The registrar may raise or lower the total pool at runtime, and any such change is applied to the free seats so that the accounting stays whole. No seat is ever created out of thin air or silently lost. The safety requirement is that free seats plus taken seats always equals the current total pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of free seats plus the number of taken seats always equals the current total seat pool, so seats are conserved.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

VARIABLES free, taken, total
vars == <<free, taken, total>>
Init == free = 2 /\ taken = 0 /\ total = 2
Enroll == free > 0 /\ free' = free - 1 /\ taken' = taken + 1 /\ UNCHANGED total
Drop == taken > 0 /\ taken' = taken - 1 /\ free' = free + 1 /\ UNCHANGED total
Expand == total < MaxTotal /\ total' = total + 1 /\ free' = free + 1 /\ UNCHANGED taken
Shrink == free > 0 /\ total' = total - 1 /\ free' = free - 1 /\ UNCHANGED taken
Next == Enroll \/ Drop \/ Expand \/ Shrink
SeatsConserved == free + taken = total

```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A power-grid load shedder allocates a small set of shed slots to feeder circuits using a two-phase commit. Each slot represents a block of load that may be shed by exactly one feeder. A feeder prepares a claim on a free slot and then commits it, at which point the slot's owner is recorded. Because prepare and commit messages can be reordered, the commit step must re-check that the slot is still free before recording ownership. Once a slot has an owner it is no longer free and cannot be handed to a second feeder. The safety requirement is that no shed slot is ever allocated to two different feeders at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every shed slot has at most one owning feeder at any time, so no slot is ever double-allocated.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m2p3t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Slots, Feeders
VARIABLES owner
vars == <<owner>>
NONE == "none"
Init == owner = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
Claim == \E s \in Slots, f \in Feeders :
             owner[s] = NONE /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = f]
Release == \E s \in Slots : owner[s] # NONE /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
Next == Claim \/ Release
SlotSingleOwner == \A s \in Slots : owner[s] = NONE \/ owner[s] \in Feeders
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
```
```cfg
CONSTANTS Slots = {s1, s2}  Feeders = {f1, f2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SlotSingleOwner
```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A container-ship crane yard performs an irreversible release: once a container is dropped from the crane onto a truck, it cannot be un-dropped. To release, the crane must hold both a coarse bay lock and a fine slot lock in that order, forming a hierarchical lock. The drop action fires at most once per container and stamps a done flag. A crane may crash silently before dropping, leaving the container held, but a crash must never cause a second drop of the same container. The system counts how many times the drop has fired. The safety requirement is that the irreversible drop fires at most once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of times the container-drop action has fired never exceeds one.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m8p5t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES coarse, fine, fired
vars == <<coarse, fine, fired>>
Init == coarse = FALSE /\ fine = FALSE /\ fired = 0
TakeCoarse == ~coarse /\ coarse' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, fired>>
TakeFine == coarse /\ ~fine /\ fine' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fired>>
Drop == coarse /\ fine /\ fired = 0 /\ fired' = 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>
Crash == coarse' = FALSE /\ fine' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED fired
Next == TakeCoarse \/ TakeFine \/ Drop \/ Crash
DropFiredOnce == fired <= 1
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
```
```cfg
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DropFiredOnce
```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A stock-exchange opening auction assigns a limited set of fill slots to brokers. A single allocation token circulates around a ring of brokers, and only the token holder may claim a currently free fill slot for itself. Each fill slot may be assigned to at most one broker. A broker may crash silently while holding the token, in which case the token can be reclaimed and passed on, but a crash must never cause a slot to be assigned twice. Once a slot is claimed its assigned broker is fixed until the auction clears. The safety requirement is that no fill slot is ever allocated to two different brokers.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every fill slot is assigned to at most one broker, so no slot is ever double-allocated.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m1p3t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS N, Slots
VARIABLES token, assign
vars == <<token, assign>>
Brokers == 0 .. (N - 1)
FREE == N
Init == token = 0 /\ assign = [s \in Slots |-> FREE]
Claim == \E s \in Slots : assign[s] = FREE /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![s] = token]
         /\ UNCHANGED token
Pass == token' = (token + 1) % N /\ UNCHANGED assign
Next == Claim \/ Pass
FillSingleBroker == \A s \in Slots : (assign[s] # FREE) => (assign[s] \in Brokers)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>An air-traffic runway allocator uses a compare-and-swap register to track how many aircraft are currently cleared onto a runway that has a fixed capacity. A controller clears an aircraft by a compare-and-swap that increments the count, but only when the count is below capacity. When an aircraft vacates the runway the count is decremented. A slow but not failed controller may lag, yet the compare-and-swap guard prevents it from clearing beyond capacity. The count never goes negative and never exceeds the runway capacity. The safety requirement is that the number of aircraft cleared onto the runway never exceeds its capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of aircraft currently on the runway never exceeds the runway capacity.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

VARIABLES onRunway
vars == <<onRunway>>
Init == onRunway = 0
Clear == onRunway < Capacity /\ onRunway' = onRunway + 1
Vacate == onRunway > 0 /\ onRunway' = onRunway - 1
Next == Clear \/ Vacate
RunwayWithinCapacity == onRunway <= Capacity
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
```

```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A stock-exchange opening auction decides how many shares to print at the opening cross, bounded by an available capacity. Each increment of the printed quantity must pass a quorum vote among matching engines: at least a majority of engines must approve before one more share prints. A privileged market-operations admin may issue an override that reduces the printed quantity for a halt, but the admin can never push the printed quantity above capacity. Votes accumulate for the next increment and reset once it is applied. The safety requirement is that the printed share quantity never exceeds the auction capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The printed share quantity never exceeds the auction's available capacity.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m5p4t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Engines, Capacity, Quorum
VARIABLES printed, approvals
vars == <<printed, approvals>>
Init == printed = 0 /\ approvals = {}
Approve == \E e \in Engines : e \notin approvals /\ approvals' = approvals \cup {e}
           /\ UNCHANGED printed
Print == Cardinality(approvals) >= Quorum /\ printed < Capacity
         /\ printed' = printed + 1 /\ approvals' = {}
AdminHalt == printed > 0 /\ printed' = printed - 1 /\ UNCHANGED approvals
Next == Approve \/ Print \/ AdminHalt
PrintWithinCap == printed <= Capacity
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
```

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PrintWithinCap
```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A smart-home door-lock network lets one guest device at a time hold an unlock lease for the front door. The lease is granted with an epoch number equal to the hub's current epoch. Each renewal advances the hub epoch and issues a fresh lease epoch. A guest device may only actuate the lock while its held lease epoch equals the hub's current epoch. A device can crash silently, but a crashed or stale device whose epoch has moved on must never actuate the lock. The hub records the epoch under which the door was last actuated. The safety requirement is that the last actuation epoch always equals the hub's current epoch, so no stale device ever unlocks the door.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The epoch of the last door actuation always equals the hub's current epoch, so no stale device ever actuates the lock.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

Actuate == held /\ leaseEpoch = epoch /\ lastActed' = epoch /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, leaseEpoch, held>>

<|start|>user<|message|>A subway signalling block system grants an irreversible movement authority into a track block: once movement authority is issued for a given block occupation, it must not be issued a second time until the block is proven clear again. A leader interlocking is elected and may fail over to a backup, and control messages between interlockings can be reordered. Only the current leader issues authority, and it records that authority has been granted. A failover must never cause a duplicate grant for the same occupation. The system counts grants issued for the current occupation. The safety requirement is that movement authority for the current occupation is granted at most once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of movement-authority grants issued for the current block occupation never exceeds one.

<|start|>user<|message|>A warehouse robot fleet limits how many robots may be simultaneously active on the floor, bounded by a fleet capacity. Activating one more robot requires a quorum of supervisor nodes to approve, so at least a majority must vote yes before an activation. A privileged floor-safety admin may issue an override that deactivates robots immediately, but can never raise the active count above the capacity. Approvals accrue toward the next activation and reset when it is applied. The safety requirement is that the number of simultaneously active robots never exceeds the fleet capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of simultaneously active robots never exceeds the fleet capacity.

<|start|>user<|message|>A pharmacy prescription dispenser guards a single narcotics drawer that only one dispensing arm may occupy at a time. Two independent dispenser instances share one physical drawer, and each arm uses a compare-and-swap on a shared occupancy register to enter. An arm may enter the drawer only when the register shows it free, atomically marking itself as the occupant; on exit it clears the register. The critical section is the physical drawer, and two arms inside it at once would be a collision. The safety requirement is that no two dispensing arms occupy the drawer at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two dispensing arms are ever inside the shared narcotics drawer at the same time.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m7p0t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Arms
VARIABLES loc
vars == <<loc>>
Init == loc = [a \in Arms |-> "idle"]
Enter == \E a \in Arms :
             loc[a] = "idle"
             /\ (\A b \in Arms : loc[b] # "drawer")
             /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![a] = "drawer"]
Exit == \E a \in Arms : loc[a] = "drawer" /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![a] = "idle"]
Next == Enter \/ Exit
DispenserMutualExclusion ==
    \A a, b \in Arms : (a # b) => ~(loc[a] = "drawer" /\ loc[b] = "drawer")
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
```

```<|return|>

Only the node whose term equals the current term may place a player, and each placement is stamped with the term under which it was made. A stale ex-leader from an older term must never place a player. The pool records the term of the most recent placement. The safety requirement is that the last placement term always equals the current term, so no stale ex-leader places players.

<|start|>user<|message|>A hospital operating-room scheduler updates a shared theatre plan using optimistic locking with retry. Each writer reads the plan's version, prepares an edit, and commits only if the version it read still matches the live version; otherwise it must retry. A privileged charge-nurse admin may force a version bump to invalidate everyone's in-flight edits. A writer holding a stale read version must never commit; it either retries against the fresh version or is rejected. The plan records the version under which the last commit landed. The safety requirement is that the version of the last committed edit always equals the live plan version, so no stale writer ever commits.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The version stamped on the last committed edit always equals the live plan version, so no writer commits against a stale version.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

Commit == readVersion = version /\ lastCommit' = version /\ version' = version + 1 /\ UNCHANGED readVersion
AdminBump == version < MaxVersion /\ version' = version + 1 /\ lastCommit' = version + 1 /\ UNCHANGED readVersion
Next == Read \/ (Commit /\ version < MaxVersion) \/ AdminBump
